official.deadline_note: Two intakes a year: the January to July intake files by 15 August (panel interview in October, results in December) and the August to December intake files by 15 March (panel interview in May, results in July). The 15 August 2026 deadline has passed, so the next filing date is 15 March 2027.
official.application_cycle: August to December intake, filing by 15 March (the January to July intake files by 15 August)
official.status_note: DOST-SEI runs two annual intakes with rolling filing deadlines; after the 15 August 2026 deadline for the January-July intake, the next filing date is 15 March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published privileges table lists 'School Fees' as covered for the FGS programme, within a 'Maximum alloted budget of Php 3,000,000.00 per scholar per academic year.'
benefits: Maximum allotted budget of Php 3,000,000.00 per scholar per academic year
Health/accident insurance, thesis/dissertation allowance, and learning materials and/or connectivity allowance
eligibility: Not more than 50 years old at the time of application
Permanent or regular employee of a private or government institution or office in the Philippines, endorsed by the Head of the Sending Institution or Office
Research interest aligned with the areas identified under the DOST's Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda (HNRDA)
Pass the admission requirements for graduate studies in a foreign university with good track record, plus the interview and other screening procedures
requirements: Undertake the MS or PhD programme on a full-time basis for a maximum period of 24 or 36 months respectively
No lateral entrant shall be considered
Make a full-time commitment to the scholarship and not engage in any form of employment during the scholarship period
Not avail or enjoy any other scholarships
Submit an advance copy of the application to fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph and the original documents to DOST-SEI at the Science Heritage Building, DOST Compound, Bicutan, Taguig City
documents: Certified True Copy of Official Transcript of Records
Endorsement from two former college professors for MS applicants, or two professors from the MS programme for PhD applicants
Recommendation from the Head of the Sending Institution or Office
Permission to take a leave of absence while on scholarship
Medical Certificate as to health status and fitness to study from a licensed physician with PRC license number indicated
Letter of Admission to the foreign university
Budgetary Requirements with supporting documents for the bases of rates used
selection_criteria: First-level screening: documentary evaluation of the application form and other requirements
Second-level screening: evaluation of the research topic and re-entry plan by the concerned DOST Council
Third-level screening: interview by a panel to be created by the SEI Director
application_method: Download the application form and list of other documentary requirements from the official DOST-SEI website
Submit an advance copy of the application to fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph before the applicable filing deadline
Submit the original documents to DOST-SEI at the Science Heritage Building, DOST Compound, Bicutan, Taguig City
Pass the three levels of screening: documentary evaluation, DOST Council evaluation of the research topic and re-entry plan, and a panel interview
official.application_route: Email an advance copy of the complete application to fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph before the filing deadline, then lodge the original documents with DOST-SEI at the Science Heritage Building, DOST Compound, Bicutan, Taguig City.
official.study_mode: Full-time (MS for a maximum of 24 months, PhD for a maximum of 36 months)
official.citizenship_residency: Filipino citizens who are permanent or regular employees of any private or government institution or office in the Philippines
official.international_eligibility: Not open to international applicants; the published criteria require Filipino citizenship.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research interest must align with the areas identified under the DOST Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda (HNRDA) and be in one of the published priority S&T fields; the scholar must enrol in a foreign university with a good track record in the specialized S&T field to be pursued.
official.research_requirement: A viable re-entry plan must be submitted as a narrative, and the research topic and re-entry plan are evaluated by the concerned DOST Council.
official.duration: Full-time MS for a maximum of 24 months; PhD for a maximum of 36 months
official.description: The DOST-SEI Foreign Graduate Scholarships in Specialized Priority Fields in Science and Technology provide opportunities for talented and deserving Filipino students to obtain MS and PhD degrees in science and engineering at reputable institutions abroad, developing a pool of high quality human resources for the country's global competitiveness and economic development.

applicant_utility.summary: This award is built for Filipino professionals who already hold a permanent or regular post: you need your head of office's endorsement and a research topic that maps onto DOST's Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda, so start with your employer rather than with the university. Treat the PHP 3,000,000 per academic year ceiling as a cap, not a promise - the Budgetary Requirements document has to justify every rate you claim with real quotes. File to the intake calendar: 15 August for a January-July start and 15 March for an August-December start, with results roughly two to four months after the panel interview.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Filipino researchers and engineers in the early years of their career who are permanently employed in the Philippines and want an MS or PhD abroad in a priority S&T field without severing their institutional ties.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the written recommendation of the Head of your Sending Institution before drafting anything else, since it is a hard requirement
Obtain the Letter of Admission from your foreign university first - the application is incomplete without it
Line up the two professor endorsements early (former college professors for MS, MS-programme professors for PhD) because they are independent of your employer
Build the Budgetary Requirements document from actual quotations from the host university so the ceiling is defensible
Book the PRC-licensed medical certificate and a valid NBI Clearance close to filing, since both are dated documents
Write the re-entry plan as a narrative tied to your current institution's needs, because the DOST Council scores it explicitly
common_rejection_risks: Lateral entry: applicants who already hold a graduate degree at the level applied for are excluded outright
Research topics that do not map onto HNRDA priority areas, which fail at the second-level DOST Council screening
A thin or generic re-entry plan, even when the research topic is strong
Missing employer recommendation or permission to take a leave of absence, which signals the sending institution is not committed
Availing of another scholarship at the same time, which is expressly prohibited
Missing the filing deadline: the advance copy must reach fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph before 15 March or 15 August, and originals must follow
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above the maximum allotted budget of PHP 3,000,000 per academic year, plus costs the published privileges do not list such as visa fees, dependants' expenses and personal travel beyond the round-trip economy airfare.
document_audit: The Transcript of Records must be a certified true copy, not a plain photocopy or a scan of one
The medical certificate must show the physician's PRC license number; a signed letter without it is routinely rejected
The NBI Clearance must be valid on the day you file, so do not obtain it months in advance
The two professor endorsements must come from the right people for your level: college professors for MS applicants, MS-programme professors for PhD applicants
The Program of Study must be consistent with the admission letter from your foreign university
Original documents must physically reach DOST-SEI in Bicutan, Taguig City, so allow courier time after emailing the advance copy
alerts: Two hard filing dates govern the whole year: 15 March for the August-December intake and 15 August for the January-July intake - miss one and you wait roughly six months
You must not engage in any form of employment during the scholarship period, which rules out consulting or remote work on the side
Results follow the panel interview by months: December for the January-July intake and July for the August-December intake
No lateral entrants are considered, so a second graduate degree in the same field is not fundable here
Placement must be at a foreign university with a good track record in the specialized field, not simply any accredited institution
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the advance copy to fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph before the filing deadline, courier the originals to the Science Heritage Building in Bicutan, Taguig City, then pass documentary screening, DOST Council evaluation of the research topic and re-entry plan, and a panel interview.
